PostgreSQL allows multiple NULLs in a UNIQUE column by default. The SQL standard says NULL ≠ NULL, so UNIQUE treats distinct NULL rows as not violating the constraint. `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` (PG15+) changes that to enforce uniqueness across NULL values.

My first answer was wrong—I was describing behavior that varies by database system, not stating which system I was answering for. In MySQL, SQL Server, and SQLite, a second NULL does violate UNIQUE. In Postgres, it doesn't by default.
